# §27 — Corrected system-flow detail sheets
**CHD-3.5 · SPEC V3.5. REVISION NOTICE — supersedes CHD-3.4 figures listed here.**
Sections 1, 5, 9, 10, 13, 14 and 21 refer to these full-size detail drawings. Legacy figure geometry is not reused for changed semantics.
This sheet set is read as a working map rather than as a decorative index. The producer is the named source of an input or proof; the controller owns durable intent, identity correlation, and reservation state; the consumer records only an effect that has passed the required readback or acceptance gate. Solid connectors show the forward handoff. Dashed and dotted connectors show held uncertainty, retry, or rework; they never imply that an absent report is a release decision.

READING KEY — PRODUCER / CONTROLLER / CONSUMER. This compact key fixes the reading direction used by every detail sheet: solid lines carry an accepted handoff, while dashed or dotted lines retain uncertainty or return work to the named owner. The labels identify who produces the record, who owns the reservation and readback, and who may consume the resulting effect.

## Detail FIGURE 1.3-1: CONTROL AUTHORITY
![FIGURE 1.3-1](../figures/fig-1.3-1.svg)
FIGURE 1.3-1 — CONTROL AUTHORITY. Snapshot: 2026-11-15.
The scheduler and Crier never write control authority. Report verification and runtime stop proof are separate paths.
1. The named initiator commits the input record before calling the adjacent adapter or evaluator. 2. The controller reads back the durable effect, correlates the response to the same identity, and only then advances the record. 3. A missing capability, mismatched correlation, lost response, or absent proof leaves the prior obligation open and records the failure branch. 4. The exact fields, calls, guards, and failure codes are the adjacent contract; an OPEN boundary is a release gate, not a dotted implementation promise.

## Detail FIGURE 9.2-1: POLICY LIFETIME
![FIGURE 9.2-1](../figures/fig-9.2-1.svg)
**FIGURE 9.2-1 — POLICY LIFETIME.** Snapshot: 2026-11-15. The left-hand producer cases enter the controller's policy decision; the right-hand consumer states distinguish a retained live snapshot, an explicit current-policy resolution, and history-only archive evidence. Restore is replacement, not fork. Missing source revision is null with a reason; effective revision is separate.
The flow is read left to right. `KEEP` is the producer/consumer handoff for an existing session, `DEFAULT` is the preserve-parent fork branch, `EXPLICIT` is the current-policy fork branch, `D-039` is the restore replacement branch, and `AUDIT` prevents archived bytes from becoming active authority.

## Detail FIGURE 13.1-1: CAPABILITY READINESS FIGURE 13.1-1 — CAPABILITY READINESS. Snapshot: 2026-11-15. The producer supplies authenticated capability evidence and the controller consumes it through separate read-only, immediate, and scheduled gates. The lower failure branch holds writes and dispatch until the fencing proof is available; a scheduler outage removes scheduled readiness but does not erase an otherwise-ready controller-local immediate path. 1. ## Detail FIGURE 13.4-1: CRIER DURABILITY AND AUTHORITY FIGURE 13.4-1 — CRIER DURABILITY AND AUTHORITY. Snapshot: 2026-11-15. The peer produces a leased delivery; the local controller consumes it only after authentication, scope mapping, durable write, and readback. Lease expiry replays the prior ACK through dedupe and creates no second effect; delivery evidence never becomes local authority, objective acceptance, or runtime capacity. 1. ## Detail FIGURE 14.3-1: ALLOCATION AND RECOVERY BEFORE / AFTER
![FIGURE 14.3-1](../figures/fig-14.3-1.svg)
FIGURE 14.3-1 — ALLOCATION AND RECOVERY BEFORE / AFTER. Snapshot: 2026-11-15.
The restored panel separates native allocation, commit readback, unknown-response reconciliation, and held capacity. The solid path identifies the normal producer-to-consumer handoff; the dashed recovery paths retain the reservation until the same identity is reconciled; the lower rework branch records the rejected report without inventing stop proof. This drawing is a reading aid for the adjacent contract, not a replacement for its fields or failure codes.
